# Graphite (vendored)

Graphite — an open source vector graphics editor and procedural design engine,
written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly.

- Source: https://github.com/GraphiteEditor/Graphite (Apache-2.0, see
  `LICENSE.txt`)
- Upstream revision built: `7af4fe4bad7aaa6437b087311879a2f1f41d85d9`
  (`master`, dated 2026-07-24, fetched 2026-07-25)
- Third-party Rust and npm dependency licences for this exact build are listed
  in `third-party-licenses.txt`, generated by upstream's own
  `cargo run -p third-party-licenses` (cargo-about 0.9.0).
- Built from source here; upstream publishes no prebuilt bundle.

## Licensing

The **source code** is Apache-2.0, which permits redistribution and
modification provided the licence and a note of changes travel with it — both
of which this file and `LICENSE.txt` provide.

Graphite's **branded assets** (its logo and its entire UI icon set) are *not*
covered by that licence. They live in a separate repository under a proprietary
branding licence which permits their use "solely as part of unmodified build
artifacts produced from the official Graphite repository" and requires that
derivative works "substitute these branded assets before distribution".

**None of those assets are downloaded, built into this bundle, or
redistributed here.** Every icon Graphite imports is instead supplied by
`scripts/build_graphite_branding.mjs`, which draws from
[Pixelarticons](https://github.com/halfmage/pixelarticons) (MIT, the same icon
family the rest of ClackOS uses) plus hand-drawn pixel glyphs in that script for
the icons Pixelarticons does not cover. The title-bar logotype is plain
monospace text, not a facsimile of the Graphite wordmark.

## Deviations from an upstream release build

1. **Substitute branding**, as above — 218 assets, none of them upstream's.
2. **Relative base path.** Built with `vite build --base ./` so the bundle
   resolves its assets from `/vendor/graphite/` rather than the site root.
3. **Service worker disabled.** Upstream registers `/service-worker.js` at
   scope `/`, which would claim the whole clacktronics.co.uk origin from inside
   an app window. The registration call in `assets/index-*.js` is patched to
   `false&&rb()` and `service-worker.js` is not shipped.
4. **Favicon and manifest links removed** from `index.html`; they pointed at
   branding files that are not redistributed, and ClackOS supplies the window
   icon anyway.
5. **Demo artwork not vendored.** Upstream's `demo-artwork/` sample documents
   are 5.2 MB and are dropped to keep the bundle down. The welcome screen's
   "Open Demo Artwork" entry is hidden by the wrapper page rather than left to
   fail; the bundle itself is untouched.

Nothing else in the bundle is modified. The ClackOS theming is applied entirely
from outside the vendor tree, by `content/applications/graphite.html` and
`assets/css/graphite-skin.css`.

## Rebuilding

Requires Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, `wasm-bindgen-cli`
(version pinned by upstream's `tools/cargo-run/src/requirements.rs`), Binaryen's
`wasm-opt`, `cargo-about` 0.9.0 and Node.js.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/GraphiteEditor/Graphite.git
cd Graphite
# Substitute the branding before anything can pull in the proprietary pack.
node /path/to/clacktronics_website/scripts/build_graphite_branding.mjs . /path/to/pixelarticons/svg
cargo run build web release            # compiles the Wasm; the Vite step is redone below
cd frontend && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=../target node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build --base ./
```

Then copy `frontend/dist/` over this directory, copy `LICENSE.txt` from the
repository root, and re-apply deviations 3 and 4.

## Size

The WebAssembly module is the bulk of it: 34 MB uncompressed, ~7.8 MB gzipped.
Upstream builds it with `opt-level=s` and keeps the Wasm name section (`wasm-opt
-O3 -g`) so its panic handler can report which node failed; that name section is
a large part of the file but is left in place here rather than diverging from
upstream's diagnostics.
